title: The domestic church (Lumen Gentium 11)
hookLine: parents as first teachers of faith at home
tomorrow: is holiness only for nuns and saints in stained glass?

cards: The rice is boiling over. The math worksheet is half done. And a seven-year-old, mid-bite, looks up and asks: where does God live?
Every grown-up at the table goes quiet. Nobody in that kitchen is ordained. There's no altar and no bell, just a pot lid rattling, and the parish office is closed till Monday.
Somebody has to say something. Vatican II's document on the Church has a name for that kitchen, and a job description for whoever answers.

teach.h: THE COUPLE: A SIGN OF CHRIST'S LOVE.
teach.b: Paragraph eleven of Lumen Gentium walks through the sacraments one by one, showing how the whole people of God lives its faith. When it reaches marriage, it slows down. First, the couple.
Christian spouses, it says, are a sign of the unity and fruitful love between Christ and the Church, and they help each other toward holiness, in married life and in raising children.
Second, the family that grows from them: children born into human society, and through baptism made children of God. Third, the name.

teach.h: THE NAME: SO TO SPEAK, A CHURCH.
teach.b: The family, the council says, is, so to speak, the domestic church. Notice the hedge: so to speak. A home isn't a parish.
But something of the Church truly happens there. Fourth, the job description.

teach.h: THE JOB: FIRST HERALDS OF FAITH.
teach.b: In this domestic church, parents are to be the first heralds of the faith to their children, by word and by example. First, before the catechist, before the priest.

And the paragraph adds that parents should encourage each child in the calling that is truly that child's own. Here's one to tell a friend tonight: the council didn't put the first teacher of faith in a pulpit.
It put that teacher at the dinner table, often with a pot boiling over.

how: In Catholic homes, families may say grace at meals, pray together at bedtime, keep a crucifix or a small prayer corner, and bless their children; parishes speak of parents as their children's first teachers in faith.

games.q: your neighbor, dad of twins, says he's "not religious enough" to teach them anything about God, so he'll leave it to religious ed. what does Lumen Gentium 11 say to him?
o: wait: first teaching belongs to trained catechists.
study theology first, then start teaching them.
he's a first herald, by word and by example.
games.why: the council calls parents the first heralds of the faith to their children, by word and example, in the family it calls the domestic church. no degree required.

practice: If someone you live with is nearby, invite them into this quiet, and say aloud together a grace some Catholic families say at meals: Bless us, O Lord, and these thy gifts, which we are about to receive from thy bounty, through Christ our Lord.
Amen. If you're alone, say the names of the people you call family, by blood or by choice, one name to a breath.

wordCard.voice: The domestic church. Lumen Gentium's so-to-speak name for a family: the place faith is first heard and seen.

orig.note: Latin in Lumen Gentium 11: the family as, so to speak, the domestic church.

carryVoice: Your line: the church at home. It meets wherever the first questions get asked. See you tomorrow.

sources.work: Second Vatican Council, Dogmatic Constitution on the Church
